Planning Nursing Services

Planning nursing services — steps, types, policies and procedures, budget and hospital design.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the steps of planning
  • Differentiate policies, procedures and protocols
  • Explain budget preparation in nursing
  • Relate planning to safe ward functioning

In simple words

Planning decides in advance what will be done, by whom, when, with what resources and how it will be checked. In a nursing unit this is the difference between a calm ward and chaos.

Steps in planning nursing services

  1. Establish objectives — how many patients, level of care
  2. Formulate alternatives — staffing, schedules, equipment plans
  3. Choose the best alternative
  4. Implement the plan
  5. Evaluate and revise

Policy, procedure, protocol

Item Meaning
Policy A standing rule that guides decisions
Procedure The steps to be followed in order
Protocol A set of rules for a specific clinical situation
Standing orders Pre-approved orders for defined situations

Budgeting for a unit

  • Prepare expenditure estimates — salaries, linen, equipment, medicines, training
  • Explain variance when actual cost differs from estimate
  • Ensure stock, indent and inventory records

🔴 A plan that is not evaluated is not a plan

Every plan needs a review point: patient outcomes, complaints, incident reports, consumption and budget variance. Plan, do, check, act.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Planning steps: objectives, alternatives, choice, implementation, evaluation.
  2. Policy guides decisions; procedure gives steps.
  3. Standing orders save time in emergencies.
  4. The nurse plans staffing, equipment, linen and stock.
  5. Budgeting estimates and controls expenditure.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Flexible planning allows changes during a crisis.
  2. Rules must be written, known and current.
  3. Work sampling and workload studies support staff estimates.
  4. Incident reports feed risk planning.
  5. Risk planning protects the patient and the nurse.

📌 Memory trick

Plan-Do-Check-Act: the Deming cycle of management.

60-second revision

  • Planning steps: objectives, alternatives, decision, action, evaluation.
  • Policies, procedures, protocols, standing orders.
  • Budgeting: salaries, linen, equipment, training.
  • Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle.
  • Evaluate to improve.

Test yourself

Planning is mainly done to:

Answer: B. Planning ensures human, material and financial resources reach the objectives on time.

A procedure in nursing is:

Answer: B. A procedure specifies the ordered steps for carrying out a task.

The Deming cycle describes:

Answer: A. Plan-Do-Check-Act (Deming) is the continual improvement cycle used in management.

Standing orders help in:

Answer: A. Standing orders are pre-approved actions for defined situations, saving critical time.

A nursing unit budget includes:

Answer: A. The unit budget covers salaries, linen, equipment, medicines and training.
